c.tagline: West Sumatra's coastal capital of rendang, sunsets, and surf-island gateways.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird operates metered taxis; insist on the meter, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front car and motorbike pricing, which is the norm for most visitors.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service. Padang lies on a seismic coast, so note tsunami evacuation routes and shelters.

avoid.reason: Watch bags in Pasar Raya market and on angkot minibuses, and note city beaches have strong currents and are best left before dark.

hood_desc: The downtown core around the Pasar Raya market, banks and offices, a short walk from the beach; the most central and convenient base for first-time visitors.
The Dutch-and-Chinese colonial old city along the Batang Arau river near Muaro harbour, with heritage warehouses, Chinatown, the Siti Nurbaya bridge and park; best for history and atmosphere.
The Taplau seafront strip (Pantai Padang/Purus), lined with beachfront hotels, sunset food stalls and the city's evening promenade; a breezy, sea-facing base.
A quieter residential and university district (Andalas/State University campuses) near the striking Grand Mosque of West Sumatra; calm and local, good for a slower pace.
The modern hotel-and-business avenue of Jalan Khatib Sulaiman, home to newer chain hotels, malls and government offices; a practical, contemporary base away from the old center.
lodging: Whiz Prime Hotel Khatib Sulaiman Padang

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; the tap supply is not potable.

transit.hours: Trans Padang BRT buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM along the Lubuk Buaya-Pasar Raya corridor; angkot run through the day, with Gojek/Grab filling late-night gaps.
transit.note: Padang has no rail metro; the backbone is the Trans Padang bus rapid transit (a single ~18 km corridor from Lubuk Buaya to Pasar Raya) alongside the colorful local angkot minibuses, plus Gojek/Grab and a commuter train (Sibinuang) running north to Pariaman.
transit.pay: Trans Padang and angkot fares are paid in cash to the conductor or driver (a few thousand rupiah); ride-hailing apps and QRIS e-wallets cover app-based trips. There is no integrated transit card.

sys.n: KA Sibinuang / Minangkabau Airport Rail Link

bus: Intercity buses from regional terminals to Bukittinggi, Pekanbaru and across Sumatra

car.idp: Recommended (International Driving Permit required alongside home license)

ferry: Teluk Bayur port and Muaro harbour: passenger ferries and fast boats to the Mentawai Islands (Siberut, Sipora, Pagai) for surfing, plus routes to Sibolga/Nias

transit.m: Minangkabau Airport Rail Link train to Padang (Simpang Haru) station (~30 min)
Damri airport bus to city center (~45 min)
Airport taxi to central Padang (30-45 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a service charge is often included at larger restaurants and hotels, and rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not expected.
